```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(arrow)
library(scales)
library(ggrepel)
library(ggbeeswarm)
library(zoo)

# ==========================================
# GOOGLE TRENDS DATA PREP
# ==========================================
all_df <- read_csv("data/clean/clean_time_series_US_6.csv")

# Convert to tidy format and rename
tidy_df <- all_df |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(matcha, chai, cold_brew, mocha, refresher, psl, smoothie),
    names_to = "keyword",
    values_to = "interest"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    keyword = recode(
      keyword,
      matcha = "Matcha",
      chai = "Chai",
      cold_brew = "Cold Brew",
      mocha = "Mocha",
      refresher = "Refresher",
      psl = "Pumpkin Spice Latte",
      smoothie = "Smoothie"
    )
  )

# Rolling 12-month average growth stat (2021 vs 2026)
growth_stats <- tidy_df |>
  arrange(keyword, time) |>
  group_by(keyword) |>

  # Get the yearly average for first and last year
  summarise(
    first_year = mean(head(interest, 12), na.rm = TRUE),
    last_year = mean(tail(interest, 12), na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_growth = if_else(
      first_year > 0,
        ((last_year - first_year) / first_year) * 100,
        NA_real_
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(pct_growth))


# Growth stability matrix info
matrix_info <- tidy_df |>
  group_by(keyword) |>
  summarise(
    volatility = sd(interest, na.rm = TRUE) / mean(interest, na.rm = TRUE),
    first_year_avg = mean(head(interest, 12), na.rm = TRUE),
    last_year_avg = mean(tail(interest, 12), na.rm = TRUE),
    growth_rate = (last_year_avg - first_year_avg) / first_year_avg,
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

median_growth <- median(matrix_info$growth_rate, na.rm = TRUE)
median_volatility <- median(matrix_info$volatility, na.rm = TRUE)

# Detrended seasonality: month divided by the trailing 12-month mean,
# then averaged by calendar month so the rising level does not
# inflate later springs.
monthly_avg <- tidy_df |>
  arrange(keyword, time) |>
  group_by(keyword) |>
  mutate(
    ttm = rollmean(interest, k = 12, align = "right", fill = NA),
    ratio = if_else(ttm > 0, interest / ttm, NA_real_),
    month = month(time, label = TRUE, abbr = TRUE)
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(ratio)) |>
  group_by(keyword, month) |>
  summarise(avg_ratio = mean(ratio), .groups = "drop")


# ==========================================
# TIKTOK DATA PREP
# ==========================================
tagged_data <- read_parquet("data/clean/clean_tiktok_data_tagged.parquet")

# Count of Content Themes. Denominator is videos, so overlapping tags
# are each a share of the corpus.
tag_counts <- tagged_data |>
  summarise(
    Starbucks = sum(starbucks),
    `Ceremonial/Traditional` = sum(traditional),
    `Flavors` = sum(flavor_innovation),
    `General` = sum(cafe_beverage)
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    everything(),
    names_to = "category",
    values_to = "count"
  ) |>
  # Calculate frequency percentage 
  mutate(percentage = count / nrow(tagged_data))

# Engagement rates use videos with at least 1,000 views.
engagement_rates <- tagged_data |>
  filter(!is.na(views), views >= 1000) |>
  select(
    views,
    engagement_rate,
    starbucks,
    traditional,
    flavor_innovation,
    cafe_beverage
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(
      starbucks,
      traditional,
      flavor_innovation,
      cafe_beverage
    ),
    names_to = "theme",
    values_to = "present"
  ) |>
  filter(present) |>
  mutate(
    theme = recode(
      theme,
      starbucks = "Starbucks",
      traditional = "Ceremonial/Traditional",
      flavor_innovation = "Flavors",
      cafe_beverage = "General"
    )
  )

theme_reach <- engagement_rates |>
  group_by(theme) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    med_eng = median(engagement_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
    med_views = median(views, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

engagement_rates <- engagement_rates |>
  left_join(theme_reach |> select(theme, n), by = "theme") |>
  mutate(theme_label = paste0(theme, "\n(n=", n, ")"))

# Percent of flavor content in Starbucks content
paired_stats <- tagged_data |>
  summarise(
    starbucks_total = sum(starbucks, na.rm = TRUE),
    overlap1 = sum(starbucks & flavor_innovation, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    pct_overlap1 = overlap1 / starbucks_total * 100
  )

# Ceremonial/Traditional engagement vs Starbucks, plus reach
reach_pair <- theme_reach |>
  filter(theme %in% c("Ceremonial/Traditional", "Starbucks"))

traditional_stat <- reach_pair |>
  select(theme, med_eng) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = theme, values_from = med_eng) |>
  mutate(multiplier = `Ceremonial/Traditional` / Starbucks) |>
  pull(multiplier)

trad_reach <- reach_pair |> filter(theme == "Ceremonial/Traditional")
sbux_reach <- reach_pair |> filter(theme == "Starbucks")
```

## Column {width="40%"}

### Growth Stability Matrix
```{r}
# Quadrant lines are the median growth rate and median CV of the seven beverages
median_growth <- median(matrix_info$growth_rate, na.rm = TRUE)
median_volatility <- median(matrix_info$volatility, na.rm = TRUE)

ggplot(matrix_info, aes(x = growth_rate, y = volatility, label = keyword)) +
  # Quadrant Lines
  geom_hline(yintercept = median_volatility, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.7, color = "gray45") + 
  geom_vline(xintercept = median_growth, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.7, color = "gray45") + 
  
  geom_point(size = 5, color = "#0077BB", alpha = 1) +
  geom_text_repel(
    # Conditional statement to set Matcha label to bold
    aes(fontface = ifelse(keyword == "Matcha", "bold", "plain")), 
    size = 4.5, 
    point.padding = 0.45, 
    box.padding = 1.2, 
    min.segment.length = 0) + 
  
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_percent(), limits = c(0, 2.5)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_percent(), limits = c(0, 1.5)) +
  
  labs(
    title = "Growth Versus Variability",
    subtitle = "Comparing rolling 12-month averages against volatility",
    x = "Long-Term Growth Rate (Trailing 12-Months vs. Baseline)",
    y = "Volatility (Coefficient of Variation)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16), 
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), 
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray90"),
    
  )
```

### Content Theme Frequency on TikTok
```{r}
ggplot(tag_counts, aes(x = reorder(category, -percentage), y = percentage, fill = category)) + 
  geom_col(alpha = 0.8) + 
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "turbo", begin = 0.2, end = 0.8) + 
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_percent()) +
  labs(
    title = "Content Theme Frequency on TikTok",
    subtitle = "Frequency of common matcha content themes across videos. \nVideos can contain multiple themes, so frequencies represent the percentage of total videos \nthat feature each tag.",
    x = "Content Theme",
    y = "Percentage of Videos"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12)
  ) + 
  geom_text(
    aes(label = percent(percentage, accuracy = 1)),
    vjust = -0.4,
    size = 4, 
    fontface = "bold",
    color = "gray30"
  )
```

```{r}
# March is matcha's peak after the trailing-year adjustment

ggplot(monthly_avg, aes(x = month, y = avg_ratio, color = keyword, group = keyword)) +

    x = "Month",

    color = "Beverage"
  ) +

    data = label_data,
    aes(label = "Matcha stays highest\nin spring"),
    nudge_y = 0.35,
    color = "gray20",
    size = 4,
    fontface = "italic",
    box.padding = 0.5
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 0.7)
  )
```

### Engagement Rate by Category Beeswarm Plot
```{r}
ggplot(engagement_rates, aes(x = reorder(theme_label, engagement_rate, FUN = median), y = engagement_rate, color = theme)) +
  geom_quasirandom(alpha = 0.6, size = 2.5, width = 0.2) +
  stat_summary(fun = median, geom = "point", shape = 15, size = 3, color = "black") +
  scale_color_viridis_d(option = "turbo", begin = 0.2, end = 0.8) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_percent()) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 0.3)) +
  labs(
    title = "Engagement Rate Distribution by Matcha Content Themes",
    subtitle = "Videos with at least 1,000 views. A video may belong to more than one theme.\nBlack square is the median. Rates above 30% are outside the axis.\nEngagement = (likes + comments + shares + saves) / views",
    x = "Content Theme",
    y = "Engagement Rate"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12)
  )
```

# Decisions
For a marketing lead at a US cafe:

**Promote matcha in spring and keep it on the menu the rest of the year.** Search interest is up 235.8% on a trailing 12-month basis, the fastest gain in this set. Variability is 0.53, above the median of about 0.21 and below pumpkin spice latte at 1.40. After removing the multi-year rise, March–May is still the high and November is still the low, at 0.87 of a normal month. Revisit this if the March–May lift disappears, or if variability rises toward 1.40.

**Put the posting budget on cafe-drink videos.** Among videos with at least 1,000 views, captions with "latte" lead both measures: 315 videos, a median of 285,800 views, and a 7.6% median engagement rate.

**Use flavor and ceremonial posts as support, not as the reach plan.** A flavor word appears in 36.1% of Starbucks-tagged videos. Inside that set, captions without a flavor word have the higher median views, 246,600 versus 91,600. Flavor-tagged videos overall have a 7.1% engagement rate and a median of 102,850 views. Ceremonial posts match the Starbucks tag on engagement at 0.97× and reach fewer people, a median of 94,000 views versus 160,850. Those Starbucks views are spread across many creators, with at most 3 videos from any one account, so they do not transfer to this brand’s own account.


# Data & Additional Info

This dashboard integrates Google Trends search data with TikTok engagement data to examine matcha as a consumer beverage, combining macro-level demand signals with social media content behavior.

**Google Trends Data**

Google Trends time-series data was collected for multiple beverage-related keywords: chai, cold brew, matcha, mocha, pumpkin spice latte, refresher, and smoothie. The dataset spans from June of 2021 to May of 2026 on a monthly resolution for the United States.

**TikTok Data**

TikTok data was collected using the Apify API based on matcha-related hashtags. The final dataset contains about 560 videos after manual removals. Each record includes engagement metrics such as views, likes, comments, shares, and saves. The Starbucks theme is the caption keyword `starbucks`. It does not cover other brands. Theme counts use every remaining video. Engagement rates use videos with at least 1,000 views.

**Theme Tagging System**

Videos were tagged with rule-based keyword detection on captions. Tags can overlap, so one video can contribute to more than one theme. Ceremonial/Traditional matches `ceremony`, `ceremonial`, `whisk`, or `chawan`. Flavors match specific words such as strawberry, ube, vanilla, coconut, banana, berry, blueberry, mango, and lavender. Broad words such as sugar, fruit, and butter are not used. The Starbucks flavor share uses this rule.

**Seasonality**

The monthly chart divides each month by that keyword’s trailing 12-month mean, then averages the ratio by calendar month. A value of 1 matches the trailing year. After this adjustment, matcha still peaks in March–May and is lowest in November.

**Growth versus variability**

Variability on the matrix is the coefficient of variation: the standard deviation of monthly search interest divided by its mean. The dashed lines are the median growth rate and the median coefficient of variation of the seven beverages. The median growth rate is about 21%, and the median coefficient of variation is about 0.21. Matcha’s coefficient of variation is 0.53, second-highest of the seven. Pumpkin spice latte is the high-variability series at 1.40. Matcha is the fastest-growing beverage in the set and sits above the median on variability.
